prompt: A serial blocking hierarchy has incremental lookup times of 4, 14 and 50 cycles for L1, L2 and L3. Their local miss rates are 10%, 40% and 25%. DRAM costs 300 additional cycles after an L3 miss. What is AMAT?

options.explanation: Correct. Nest the lower-level average into each upper-level miss penalty, using local rates.
This is the L3-and-below average service time paid after an L2 miss, not the average across every L1 access.
This is the L2-and-below average paid only when L1 misses.
Adding every lookup and DRAM cost treats every demand access as missing every level.

workedExample:
Start at L3 and work upwards.

```formula
A_3 = 50 cycles + 0.25 × 300 cycles
A_3 = 125 cycles
A_2 = 14 cycles + 0.40 A_3
A_2 = 64 cycles
A_1 = 4 cycles + 0.10 A_2
A_1 = 10.4 cycles
where
A_3: average service time of an access reaching L3, in clock cycles
A_2: average service time of an access reaching L2, in clock cycles
A_1: average service time of all demand accesses at L1, in clock cycles
cycles: processor clock cycles
In words: only the accesses missing a level pay its lower-level average, producing 10.4 cycles per demand access.
```
